Las Vegas Strip Revenue Barely Rises in August as Tourism Keeps Slowing

Published October 4, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Las Vegas Strip casinos generated $684.1 million in gaming revenue in August, according to the Nevada Gaming Control Board's August 2026 report released September 30 — up just 0.7% from a year earlier, even as several of the Strip's core games posted sharp declines. Statewide, Nevada casinos brought in $1.26 billion across 314 licensed locations, up 3.1% year over year.

Baccarat masked weakness almost everywhere else

The Strip's flat headline number hid a lot of movement underneath. Blackjack revenue fell 20%, roulette dropped 39.5%, sports betting revenue on the Strip fell 32%, and penny slots declined 22.5% compared to August 2025. Offsetting nearly all of that was baccarat, where revenue jumped 34% to $155 million — driven not by more money being bet, but by a hold rate of 18.5%, far above the 10.5% hold the game produced a year earlier. The report notes the amount actually wagered on baccarat was lower than last August; the swing was in how much of it the house happened to keep, which can vary sharply from month to month in a high-stakes game with relatively few hands played.

Downtown Las Vegas revenue slipped 3% to $61.5 million, with declines across nearly every table game except Let It Ride. Over the trailing 12 months, Strip revenue totaled nearly $9 billion, up 1.5% — a far more modest pace than the growth the market posted in recent years.

Visitor volume and hotel rates both fell

The Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority reported roughly 3.03 million visitors in August, a 4.3% year-over-year decline that it attributed partly to a lighter event calendar and to Labor Day weekend falling mostly in September this year rather than August. Hotel occupancy fell to 74.1%, down 3.4 percentage points, and the average daily room rate dropped 7.4% to $150.32, as resorts leaned on discounting — including a multi-property "Vegas 5-Day Sale" — to fill rooms. Passenger traffic at Harry Reid International Airport fell 9% year over year. Convention attendance was a bright spot, climbing 6% to about 622,700 attendees.

Speaking at the Global Gaming Expo in Las Vegas this week, MGM Resorts CEO Bill Hornbuckle pushed back on the narrative that the city has lost its value proposition: "We've all seen these cycles; I think it will return. As it relates to value, I think the market and the city have adjusted well." He added that Las Vegas hotel rates remain well below comparable markets: "We're still 40% lower than New York... We're 7% lower than Los Angeles. Las Vegas is still an incredible value."

Why it matters to bettors and players

Softer visitor volume and flat gaming revenue don't change the math at any individual table or machine, but they help explain the wave of room-rate discounting and promotional pushes resorts have leaned into this year. For players tracking the broader health of the Las Vegas market — as opposed to any single property's marketing — the gap between a nearly flat headline revenue number and double-digit declines in blackjack, roulette, and slots is the more telling detail than the topline figure alone.

Sources

  • Casino.org — "Las Vegas Casino Revenue Stalls in August Amid Persistent Tourism Headwinds"
